want.now.why: No io: the -o of voglio already says who. imparare follows with no 'to', and language names take the article: il khasi.

want.past.why: Tense sits on the door: volevo is imperfetto, the natural past for a wish. Ho voluto (passato prossimo) would mean I actually set out to.

want.neg.why: One-piece negation: non goes straight in front of the door. No do-support and no second word like French pas.

want.q.why: Same order as a statement; only rising pitch makes it a question. No tu either: the -i ending of vuoi already means you.

decline.now.why: Both subjects are dropped: posso and devo carry the person. perché leaves the second clause in plain main-clause order.

decline.past.why: Passato prossimo for the one-off failure, imperfetto dovevo for the standing duty. Textbooks prefer sono potuto (venire takes essere); ho potuto is common speech.

decline.fut.why: Future is a suffix on each door: potrò, dovrò. No 'be able to' swap. In speech the present often does it: domani non posso, devo lavorare.

decline.although.why: anche se takes the plain indicative (devo). The textbook benché would force the subjunctive: benché debba lavorare.

like.now.why: Back to front, like Hindi: il caffè is the grammatical subject and mi (to me) is the liker, so piace agrees with the coffee.

like.neg.why: non goes before the whole mi piace block, never between mi and piace. The article stays: il caffè means coffee in general.

like.she.why: Only the pronoun changes, mi to le (to her). piace stays the same because it agrees with il caffè, not with her.

like.q.why: ti (to you) replaces mi; word order is identical to the statement and rising pitch does the asking.

go.habit.why: a + il fuses into al, so al mercato is one unit. No io: vado alone means I go. Ogni giorno is an equally common time phrase.

go.prog.why: A real progressive: stare + gerund (sto andando), close to English am going. It is optional; vado al mercato can also mean right now.

go.past.why: andare takes essere, not avere: sono andato. The participle agrees with the speaker, andata for a woman.

go.fut.why: Speech keeps the present and lets domani carry the future. The synthetic future andrò al mercato is also common, with tense as a suffix.

go.neg.why: Plain present with non before it: non sto andando is grammatical but rare, so non vado covers I'm not going.

live.now.why: Present plus da: literally I live here from two years. No perfect and no auxiliary; da alone says it started and is still true.

live.past.why: Finished stretch: passato prossimo with avere (ho abitato) and da becomes per. Speech often drops per: ho abitato lì due anni.

live.fut.why: Not a future perfect: the future goes on saranno (it will be) three years, che links, abito stays present. Avrò abitato sounds bookish.

live.q.why: The question phrase comes first and the verb is plain present abiti: da quanto tempo is the question form of da due anni.

if.real.why: se + present, future viaggerò in the main clause: the -rò ending is English will. Both subjects dropped; no article on tempo.

if.unreal.why: se + congiuntivo imperfetto (avessi), condizionale (viaggerei) in the main clause. Se avrei is the classic mistake to avoid.

if.past.why: Both halves are avere + participle: avessi avuto (subjunctive), avrei viaggiato (conditional). Speech often says se avevo tempo, viaggiavo.
